question.text: In a 'full (100%) catch-up' waterfall with 8% hurdle + 80/20 carry after catch-up, at the catch-up stage:

answer.text: The GP receives 50% of distributions until its cumulative share equals 20% of cumulative profits.
The GP receives 100% of distributions until its cumulative share equals 20% of cumulative profits including the hurdle portion.

explanation.text: The Logic: A 100% catch-up means the GP receives 100% of all distributions during the catch-up tier until the GP's cumulative take equals 20% of total profits (hurdle amount + catch-up). After that, the 80/20 split kicks in on the remainder. The Trap: 50% describes a slower 'half catch-up'. 0% is post-hurdle pre-catch-up misconception. 80% would bypass the catch-up concept. Cross-Exam Context: Ch 6 Fee Structure and XIX-C extensively cover the math. XIX-D tests manager-side drafting choices. Manager's Pro-Tip: LPs increasingly push back on 100% catch-up; a 50%-50% catch-up is gaining ground in 2024-25 LP negotiations. Know the economics of each before drafting the PPM.
